more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
Approved in the US.
US food use is subject to the listed CFR provisions and their conditions, checked in 2026.
more_info.overview: Propylene glycol, chemically propane-1,2-diol, is a two-hydroxyl alcohol used as a carrier and in other specified food-processing functions. Its moisture-control role is to help prevent a food from drying out. The specified material is supplied as colourless liquid. The specification identifies water solubility as one of its properties.
more_info.side_effects:
Refined estimates from assessed food uses stayed below the limit.
The opinion found no reason to revise the existing intake limit.
more_info.origin: FDA describes synthetic manufacture through a propylene chlorohydrin intermediate, followed by conversion to the glycol, or by heating glycerol with sodium hydroxide. These are chemical routes for propane-1,2-diol. The regulation does not establish the feedstock source of every glycerol batch.
